svg.text: Three ways to prove you own a name: ACME HTTP-01, TLS-ALPN-01, DNS-01
What the CA checks, and where the proof lives · Sprint 3, Day 3 side quest of my NGINX learning journey
1 Every challenge sits inside the same ACME order
send a CSR for the names
key authorization = token + "." + base64url(SHA-256 thumbprint of the account public key)
Every proof below is built from it, so a copied token is useless to anyone else's ACME account.
2 HTTP-01: serve a file on port 80
Port 80 must be reachable from the internet. No wildcards.
nginx-module-acme answers before the rewrite phase, so a blanket return 301 doesn't block it (lab B.1).
Behind a load balancer, every node must answer, or forward /.well-known/acme-challenge/ to the one that can.
3 TLS-ALPN-01: answer a special handshake on port 443
build a challenge cert for lumina.local
Port 443 only, so it fits edges with no port 80. No wildcards.
Whatever terminates TLS in front of the ACME client must pass acme-tls/1 through to it.
A BIG-IP virtual server that terminates TLS in front of NGINX breaks it unless it hands that ALPN on.
The only challenge that issues wildcards (*.lumina.local), and the only one for names with no public web server.
A CNAME from _acme-challenge to a zone used only for ACME limits what those credentials can change.
nginx-module-acme 0.4.1 has no DNS-01 solver. On BIG-IP, kojot-acme does DNS-01.
ACMEv2 = RFC 8555 · TLS-ALPN-01 = RFC 8737 · Lab: Pebble test CA + nginx-module-acme 0.4.1 on nginx 1.31.6
